items.stem: OSPF neighbours on a point-to-point link reach EXSTART/EXCHANGE but never FULL. Which cause is most likely?

options.text: MTU mismatch between the two interfaces
options.rationale: Correct: an MTU mismatch stalls the database exchange at EXSTART/EXCHANGE.
Process IDs are locally significant and do not prevent adjacency.
Timer mismatch prevents reaching even 2-WAY/EXSTART, not stalling at EXCHANGE.
Bandwidth affects cost, not adjacency formation.

items.explanation: Correct: an MTU mismatch stalls the database exchange at EXSTART/EXCHANGE.

items.stem: A DMVPN spoke cannot build a spoke-to-spoke tunnel though both reach the hub. Which component should you check first?

options.rationale: Correct: spoke-to-spoke tunnels depend on NHRP resolving the peer's NBMA address.
Hub reachability already works, so the hub default route is not the blocker.
Console access is unrelated to tunnel establishment.
Shaping may affect performance but does not stop tunnel resolution.

items.explanation: Correct: spoke-to-spoke tunnels depend on NHRP resolving the peer's NBMA address.

items.stem: Which TWO actions help a Control Plane Policing (CoPP) policy protect the router without breaking operations? (Select TWO)

options.text: Permit routing-protocol traffic to the control plane
options.rationale: Correct: routing protocols must reach the control plane or adjacencies drop.

options.text: Rate-limit management traffic such as SSH and SNMP
options.rationale: Correct: rate-limiting management protects the CPU from floods while allowing access.

options.text: Drop all traffic destined to the control plane
options.rationale: Dropping everything would break routing and management entirely.

options.text: Apply the policy only to transit data traffic
options.rationale: CoPP protects control-plane traffic, not transit data.

items.explanation: Correct: routing protocols must reach the control plane or adjacencies drop. Correct: rate-limiting management protects the CPU from floods while allowing access.
